question: I'm a BA junior (P-025) with dual Finance and BAT concentrations and an Economics minor. Can 73-102 (Microeconomics) count toward both my Finance concentration and my Economics minor?

domain_contributions.programs: Finance concentration: 73-102 may appear as a required or elective course. Economics minor: 73-102 (Microeconomics) is a standard Economics minor foundation course
domain_contributions.courses: 73-102 (9 units) — its content directly overlaps between Finance and Economics; the double-counting question is whether both programs can claim it

key_facts: 73-102 is foundational for both Economics (minor) and Finance (concentration) content
CMU's double-counting policy generally prohibits a course from satisfying requirements in two separate programs (major concentration AND minor)
The specific Finance concentration requirements and Economics minor requirements need cross-referencing
P-025's advisor must decide which program receives credit for 73-102
wrong_if_single_domain: Looking only at Finance concentration requirements might accept 73-102. Looking only at Econ minor requirements would also accept it. Only by combining both program views does the double-counting conflict emerge.
common_mistake: Counting 73-102 toward both Finance and Economics simultaneously, unknowingly reducing the effective course requirements for one of the programs
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs, Finance): Is 73-102 required/accepted for Finance concentration? → likely yes
Step 2 (programs, Econ minor): Is 73-102 required for Econ minor? → yes (foundational)
Step 3 (policies): Double-counting restriction → one course, one program
Conclusion: 73-102 can satisfy either Finance concentration or Econ minor, but not both — P-025 needs an additional Econ course if 73-102 goes to Finance
